answer: In an agent economy, each participant locks a refundable stake tied to one unique credential and signs every vote with it. A web of trust then weights attestations by that stake. A sybil can try to whisper fake identities into the network, but each new account must post real collateral, so the attacker pays for every vote. Honest agents cross-check and slash anyone caught recycling the same fable across many names. That drains the oasis of free reputation: to sway a vote the attacker must risk more capital than the honest coalition, making identity fraud a losing trade.
